tasks.title: Target Audience & Customer Persona Research
tasks.what: Create a clear profile of your ideal buyer—including their biggest problem, buying triggers, objections, and favorite online channels.
tasks.why: When you know exactly who you are talking to and what problems keep them awake, your ads and posts get 2x–3x more clicks at a lower cost.
tasks.when: Before launching any new product, campaign, or quarterly marketing plan (and reviewed monthly).
tasks.tools: Customer Surveys, Google Analytics, Reviews (Trustpilot / Shopee / Lazada / Amazon), AnswerThePublic
steps: Read 20 recent 5-star and 1-star customer reviews in your product category to spot exact phrases buyers use.
Write down the top 3 problems your customer wants to solve and the #1 reason they hesitate to buy.
List the top 2 platforms where this buyer spends time daily (e.g., TikTok & Shopee in PH, LinkedIn & Google in B2B US/UK).
Summarize this into a 1-page Customer Persona card for your team.
tasks.expected: A 1-page Customer Persona profile with 3 pain points, 3 buying triggers, and top channels.
tasks.measure: Higher Click-Through Rate (CTR) and lower Cost Per Lead/Sale on campaigns written for this persona.
tasks.mistakes: Guessing what customers want without reading real reviews or making the audience 'everyone aged 18–65'.
tasks.example: Persona: 'Busy Working Parent in Metro Manila / London' — Wants: 15-minute healthy dinner kits; Objection: Worried about delivery freshness; Channel: Instagram Reels & Google Search.

tasks.title: Competitor Offer, Ad & Funnel Analysis
tasks.what: Review the top 3 competitors in your market to see what ads they are running, how they price their offer, and how their landing page converts visitors.
tasks.why: Shows you what is already working in your market and reveals gaps where your brand can stand out.
tasks.when: Once a month and before launching a major seasonal promotion.
tasks.tools: Meta Ad Library, Google Ads Transparency Center, TikTok Creative Center, Similarweb
steps: Look up your top 3 competitors inside the free Meta Ad Library and Google Ads Transparency Center.
Find ads they have kept running for 30+ days (long-running ads are usually profitable).
Click through their landing page and sign up for their email list to see their follow-up sequence.
Write down 2 strengths to learn from and 2 weaknesses your offer solves better.
tasks.expected: A comparison table of 3 competitors showing their headline, offer/bonus, pricing, and ad hooks.
tasks.measure: New differentiated ad angles that beat your baseline click rate by 15–25%.
tasks.mistakes: Copying a competitor's ad word-for-word instead of highlighting what makes your offer stronger.
tasks.example: Competitor charges $15 shipping with 5-day delivery; we highlight 'Free Next-Day Shipping + 30-Day Guarantee' in our headline.

tasks.title: Customer Journey & Funnel Stage Mapping
tasks.what: Map out the 3 steps a stranger takes from first discovering your brand (Awareness), to trusting you (Consideration), to buying (Conversion).
tasks.why: Most people do not buy the very first time they see an ad. Mapping the journey ensures you follow up at every stage.
tasks.when: At the start of each quarter or when launching a new product line.
tasks.tools: Notion / Google Docs, Tab 02 Campaign Planner, Google Analytics Funnel Report
steps: Step 1 (Awareness): Choose content that attracts cold audiences (short videos, helpful blog guides, search ads).
Step 2 (Consideration): Offer a low-risk next step (free sample, price guide, case study, customer reviews).
Step 3 (Conversion): Present a clear offer with urgency, trust badges, and simple checkout or booking.
Assign 1 metric to measure each stage (Reach -> Clicks/Leads -> Sales).
tasks.expected: A complete 3-stage marketing funnel diagram with matching content and ads for each step.
tasks.measure: Steady increase in returning visitor conversion rate and overall sales.
tasks.mistakes: Showing hard-sell 'Buy Now' ads to cold strangers without any proof or education.
tasks.example: Stage 1: 30s TikTok tip video -> Stage 2: Free PDF buying guide via email -> Stage 3: 10% first-order welcome voucher.

tasks.title: Google Ads Search Term Cleanup & Negative Keywords
tasks.what: Review the exact search phrases people typed into Google before clicking your paid ads, and block unrelated words.
tasks.why: Stops you from paying for accidental clicks from people looking for freebies, jobs, or unrelated products.
tasks.when: Twice a week for new campaigns; once a week for established campaigns.
steps: Open Google Ads and navigate to Campaigns -> Insights and Reports -> Search Terms.
Sort by 'Cost' from highest to lowest over the last 7 to 14 days.
Select any unrelated search phrases (e.g., 'free', 'salary', 'repair manual') and click 'Add as negative keyword'.
Take high-converting search phrases and add them as Exact or Phrase match keywords.
tasks.expected: A cleaner search campaign where 90%+ of paid clicks come from high-intent buyers.
tasks.measure: 10% to 25% lower Cost Per Acquisition (CPA) and higher Conversion Rate.
tasks.mistakes: Using broad match keywords without adding negative keywords, which burns budget rapidly.
tasks.example: An online accounting software company blocks 'accounting jobs' and 'free excel template', saving $450/month in wasted clicks.

tasks.title: Meta (Facebook/Instagram) & TikTok Ad Creative Testing
tasks.what: Launch and compare 3 different video or image ad angles to see which hook captures attention and drives the lowest cost per sale.
tasks.why: On social media, your creative (video/image) drives 70%+ of ad performance. Fresh hooks prevent ad fatigue.
tasks.when: Every week or whenever ad click rates drop and costs rise.
tasks.tools: Meta Ads Manager, TikTok Ads Manager, CapCut, Canva
steps: Prepare 3 distinct ad concepts: (A) Problem/Solution demo, (B) Customer review/unboxing, (C) Before & After comparison.
Make the first 3 seconds visually engaging with clear on-screen headline text.
Run all 3 ads with equal budget for 3 to 5 days before turning off the losers.
Scale budget on the winning ad that beats your target Cost Per Sale.
tasks.expected: 1 to 2 winning video or carousel ads that bring consistent daily sales within your target margin.
tasks.measure: Link Click-Through Rate (CTR) above 1.5% and Return on Ad Spend (ROAS) above your break-even target.
tasks.mistakes: Turning off an ad after only 3 hours or changing 5 things at once so you don't know what worked.
tasks.example: Hook A ('Tired of back pain at your desk?') got a 2.8% CTR and $12 CPA vs Hook B's 0.9% CTR.

tasks.title: B2B LinkedIn Lead Generation & Account Targeting
tasks.what: Run targeted campaigns reaching decision-makers by Job Title, Industry, and Company Size on LinkedIn.
tasks.why: For B2B and high-ticket services, LinkedIn lets you put your offer directly in front of verified managers, directors, and founders.
tasks.when: Weekly optimization during active B2B lead generation campaigns.
tasks.tools: LinkedIn Campaign Manager, HubSpot / Salesforce CRM
steps: Filter audience by specific Job Titles or Seniority (e.g., HR Director, Operations Manager) and Company Size (50–500 employees).
Disable 'Audience Expansion' so LinkedIn doesn't show ads outside your strict buyer criteria.
Offer a high-value industry benchmark report, ROI calculator, or live demo using LinkedIn Lead Gen Forms.
Sync leads automatically to your CRM for a 15-minute sales follow-up.
tasks.expected: Qualified business leads with verified work emails, company names, and job titles.
tasks.measure: Cost Per Qualified Lead (CPQL) and percentage of leads that book a discovery call.
tasks.mistakes: Sending cold B2B traffic to a generic 'Contact Us' page instead of a specific case study or value offer.
tasks.example: Offering a '2026 Warehouse Automation Cost Guide' generated 42 qualified Operations Director leads at $38/lead.

tasks.title: Daily Budget Pacing & Break-Even ROAS Check
tasks.what: Check daily ad spending across all platforms to make sure you neither overspend your monthly budget nor run ads below your break-even profit margin.
tasks.why: Prevents costly billing surprises and protects your net profit margin.
tasks.tools: Tab 04 Break-Even & ROAS Calculator, Google Ads, Meta Ads
steps: Calculate your true Break-Even ROAS in Tab 04 using your actual product profit margin.
Check yesterday's spend and ROAS across Google, Meta, TikTok, or LinkedIn.
Pause ad sets that spent 2x your target Cost Per Sale with 0 conversions.
Increase budget by no more than 15–20% at a time on profitable campaigns.
tasks.expected: Controlled monthly ad spend within +/- 3% of plan and positive net profit after ad costs.
tasks.measure: Net Profit ROI (%) and actual spend vs. planned monthly budget.
tasks.mistakes: Doubling an ad set's budget overnight (which resets the ad platform's learning phase) or ignoring product costs.
tasks.example: With a 50% gross margin, your Break-Even ROAS is 2.0x. Any campaign above 2.8x ROAS is generating healthy net profit.

tasks.title: High-Intent Keyword Research & Search Intent Mapping
tasks.what: Find the exact phrases customers type into Google when they are ready to compare options or buy.
tasks.why: Ranking for 1 buyer-intent phrase (like 'best CRM for small agencies') brings more sales than 10 vague topics.
tasks.when: Monthly when planning new website pages and blog articles.
tasks.tools: Google Keyword Planner, Google Search Console, Ahrefs / Semrush / Ubersuggest
steps: List 10 core products or services you offer and pair them with buyer words ('best', 'pricing', 'review', 'near me').
Check monthly search volume and competition in Google Keyword Planner.
Group similar keywords together so 1 strong page targets 1 main topic.
Match your page type to what currently ranks on Page 1 (product page, comparison guide, or calculator).
tasks.expected: A prioritized list of 10–20 target keywords mapped to specific website pages.
tasks.measure: Top 10 Google rankings and month-over-month growth in non-branded organic clicks.
tasks.mistakes: Creating multiple weak pages targeting the exact same keyword (keyword cannibalization).
tasks.example: Targeting 'emergency plumber Pasig 24/7' on a dedicated service page with clear pricing and a click-to-call button.

tasks.title: On-Page SEO Audit (Titles, Headings, Internal Links & Alt Text)
tasks.what: Optimize your page title, H1 heading, subheadings, image descriptions, and internal links so Google and readers immediately understand the page.
tasks.why: Simple on-page updates often jump a page from position #12 (Page 2) to position #4 (Page 1) within weeks.
tasks.when: Every time you publish a new page and weekly for existing top pages.
tasks.tools: Google Search Console, Yoast / RankMath, Screaming Frog
steps: Place your primary keyword near the front of the Page Title (<60 chars) and H1 Heading.
Write a compelling Meta Description (<155 chars) with a clear benefit so searchers click your link.
Add descriptive alt text to images and compress them to WebP format.
Add 3 internal links from your existing high-traffic pages pointing to the new page.
tasks.expected: 100% of priority landing pages have unique titles, fast images, and strong internal links.
tasks.measure: Higher organic Click-Through Rate (CTR) and average position in Google Search Console.
tasks.mistakes: Leaving default titles like 'Home - Company Name' or stuffing keywords unnaturally into every sentence.
tasks.example: Changing title from 'Services' to 'Commercial Solar Installation in Melbourne — Free Site Quote' lifted organic clicks by 48%.

tasks.title: Landing Page Speed & Conversion Rate Optimization (CRO)
tasks.what: Make your landing page load in under 3 seconds on mobile and remove friction so more visitors turn into buyers or leads.
tasks.why: Doubling your conversion rate from 1.5% to 3.0% doubles your sales without spending a single extra dollar or peso on ads.
tasks.when: Monthly review of your top 5 highest-traffic landing pages.
tasks.tools: Google PageSpeed Insights, Microsoft Clarity (free heatmaps & recordings)
steps: Open your landing page on a smartphone and check if the main headline, benefit, and button are visible without scrolling.
Place real customer reviews, star ratings, or client logos right next to your call-to-action button.
Watch 10 session recordings in Microsoft Clarity to see where mobile users get stuck or drop off.
Remove non-essential form fields so checkout or lead signup takes under 45 seconds.
tasks.expected: A fast, mobile-friendly landing page with clear trust signals and a frictionless checkout/form.
tasks.measure: Landing page Conversion Rate (CVR %) and bounce rate reduction.
tasks.mistakes: Sending paid ad traffic to a slow homepage with 15 different menu links instead of 1 focused offer page.
tasks.example: Cutting a B2B quote form from 9 fields down to 4 fields increased completed lead submissions by 37%.

tasks.title: Google Analytics 4 (GA4) & Conversion Tracking Check
tasks.what: Verify that every purchase, lead form submission, phone click, or chat inquiry is accurately recorded in Google Analytics 4 and your ad platforms.
tasks.why: If conversion tracking breaks, you and your ad algorithms are flying blind and cannot tell which ads bring real revenue.
tasks.when: Weekly and immediately after any website or checkout update.
tasks.tools: Google Analytics 4 (GA4), Google Tag Manager, Meta Pixel Helper
steps: Complete a real test signup or test order on your website using your mobile phone.
Confirm the conversion event fires once (and not twice) in GA4 Realtime / DebugView.
Compare total orders/leads in GA4 against your actual store backend (Shopify, WooCommerce, CRM).
Ensure cookie consent banners (GDPR in UK/EU) properly pass consent signals.
tasks.expected: Accurate, deduplicated conversion tracking within 5% of actual backend orders/leads.
tasks.measure: Tracking accuracy % between backend sales records and analytics dashboard.
tasks.mistakes: Counting every 'Page View' as a conversion instead of tracking only the final 'Thank You / Order Confirmed' action.
tasks.example: Fixing a broken Thank-You page tag revealed that Email newsletters were driving 30% more purchases than previously reported.

tasks.title: UTM Tracking Link Standardization for All Campaigns
tasks.what: Attach consistent UTM tracking tags to every link you share in emails, social media bios, QR codes, and paid ads.
tasks.why: Without UTM tags, Google Analytics lumps your social media and email clicks into 'Direct / Unknown' traffic.
tasks.when: Every time you publish a campaign link (use the built-in UTM Builder in Tab 02!).
tasks.tools: Tab 02 Built-In UTM Builder, Google Analytics Traffic Acquisition Report
steps: Open Tab 02 (Campaign & Content Hub) and scroll to the built-in UTM Link Builder.
Enter your website URL, Traffic Source (e.g., `instagram`, `newsletter`), Medium (`social`, `email`, `cpc`), and Campaign Name (`summer_sale`).
Always use lowercase letters and underscores so Analytics doesn't split `Facebook` and `facebook` into two rows.
Copy the generated tracking link and test it in your browser before posting.
tasks.expected: 100% of campaign links tagged with clean, lowercase UTM parameters.
tasks.measure: Unassigned / Direct traffic share drops below 10% in Google Analytics.
tasks.mistakes: Using UTM tags on internal links inside your own website (which overwrites the original traffic source!).

tasks.title: Monthly Executive Performance Report & ROI Summary
tasks.what: Compile a clear 1-page monthly report showing Total Spend, Total Revenue/Leads, ROAS/ROI, Top 3 Wins, and Next Month's Action Plan.
tasks.why: Clients and managers don't want 40 pages of raw charts—they want to know what money was spent, what returned, and what you are doing next.
tasks.when: First business day of every month.
tasks.tools: Tab 02 Monthly Report Generator, Google Looker Studio, Google Analytics
steps: Gather total marketing spend, total revenue, and total leads/customers for the month.
Use the Tab 02 Monthly Report Generator to calculate blended ROAS, CPA, and conversion rate automatically.
List the Top 3 winning campaigns/posts and Top 2 lessons learned from underperforming tests.
Outline 3 concrete priorities for the upcoming month and export/print as a clean PDF.
tasks.expected: A concise, plain-English 1-page Monthly Marketing Report ready for clients or leadership.
tasks.measure: Stakeholder approval, clear budget decisions, and consistent month-over-month efficiency gains.
tasks.mistakes: Reporting only 'vanity metrics' (likes and impressions) without connecting them to leads, sales, or revenue.
tasks.example: 'In October we invested $4,200 across Google & Meta Ads, generating 140 new customers and $18,900 in revenue (4.5x ROAS).'

tasks.title: Automated Welcome & Abandoned Cart Email/SMS Flows
tasks.what: Set up and test automated messages that greet new subscribers immediately and remind shoppers who left items in their cart.
tasks.why: Automated flows work 24/7 in the background and typically generate 25% to 40% of total email marketing revenue.
tasks.when: Set up once, then review and A/B test subject lines monthly.
steps: Email 1 (Sent immediately on signup): Deliver the promised welcome gift/guide and share your brand story.
Email 2 (Sent 24 hours later): Highlight your best-selling products or top 3 customer case studies.
Abandoned Cart Flow (Sent 1 hour & 20 hours after cart exit): Show the exact item left behind with a direct link back to checkout.
Verify opt-in consent and include a 1-click Unsubscribe link in every footer (required by GDPR/CAN-SPAM).
tasks.expected: Live 3-part Welcome Flow and 2-part Abandoned Cart/Lead Follow-Up Flow.
tasks.measure: Click-Through Rate (CTR %) and Revenue or Bookings per recipient (avoid relying solely on Open Rate due to Apple Mail Privacy Protection).
tasks.mistakes: Sending a discount code in the very first hour of cart abandonment (which trains customers to abandon carts on purpose).
tasks.example: A 2-step Abandoned Cart flow recovered 14% of unfinished checkouts, adding ₱85,000 / $1,500 in monthly sales automatically.

tasks.title: Customer Segmentation (VIP Buyers, First-Timers & Win-Back)
tasks.what: Group your customer list by buying behavior so VIP customers get early access, first-time buyers get usage tips, and inactive buyers get a win-back offer.
tasks.why: Segmented emails generate 3x higher click rates and half as many unsubscribes compared to blasting the same email to everyone.
tasks.when: Monthly list segmentation and hygiene check.
tasks.tools: Klaviyo, HubSpot, Salesforce, Shopify Customer Segments
steps: Create Segment 1 (VIPs): Customers who bought 3+ times or spent in the top 15%.
Create Segment 2 (Warm Prospects): Subscribers who clicked an email in the last 30 days but haven't bought yet.
Create Segment 3 (Win-Back): Past buyers who haven't ordered in 60–90 days.
Suppress unengaged addresses (no clicks in 120+ days) to keep inbox deliverability high.
tasks.expected: 4 clean customer segments in your CRM/email platform with tailored messaging.
tasks.measure: Repeat purchase rate (%), revenue per email recipient, and spam complaint rate under 0.08%.
tasks.mistakes: Blasting daily promo emails to cold inactive contacts, which pushes your domain into the Gmail/Yahoo Spam folder.
tasks.example: Giving the VIP segment 24-hour early access to a new product launch generated 40% of launch-week sales with $0 ad spend.

tasks.title: Short-Form Vertical Video Production (TikTok, Reels & Shorts)
tasks.what: Script, film, and caption 3 to 5 short vertical videos (15–45 seconds) that educate, entertain, or demonstrate your product in action.
tasks.why: Short vertical video is the #1 organic reach engine across TikTok, Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts, and Facebook.
tasks.tools: Smartphone Camera, CapCut, Canva, TikTok / Instagram App
steps: Hook (0–3 seconds): Start with a bold question, surprising visual, or specific customer problem.
Value / Demo (3–25 seconds): Show the step-by-step fix or product demonstration with fast cuts every 3–4 seconds.
Captions: Add large, high-contrast captions in the center safe zone so 80% of sound-off viewers can read along.
Call to Action (Last 4 seconds): Tell viewers one clear next step ('Comment GUIDE' or 'Tap the link in our bio').
tasks.expected: 3–5 ready-to-post vertical videos with captions and strong 3-second hooks.
tasks.measure: 3-Second Hold Rate (>30%), Average Watch Time, Saves/Shares, and profile link clicks.
tasks.mistakes: Starting videos with a slow 5-second logo intro or 'Hi guys, welcome back'—which causes viewers to swipe away immediately.
tasks.example: Starting a video with '3 mistakes costing small restaurants 20% of their delivery orders' reached 48,000 local viewers organically.

tasks.title: Content Repurposing & Multi-Channel Scheduling
tasks.what: Turn 1 core weekly topic (a blog guide, podcast, or customer case study) into 6+ pieces of content across social media and email.
tasks.why: Saves 10+ hours a week while keeping your brand message consistent across every platform.
tasks.when: Every Monday or Tuesday during weekly content planning.
tasks.tools: Canva, Buffer / Meta Business Suite / Later, Tab 02 Content Planner
steps: Start with 1 high-value topic that answers a major customer question.
Create 1 swipeable 5-slide carousel for Instagram & LinkedIn summarizing the main steps.
Film 2 short 30-second vertical videos covering tip #1 and tip #2.
Adapt the summary into your Thursday email newsletter and schedule all posts for peak hours.
tasks.expected: A full week of scheduled posts across 3–4 platforms built from a single research topic.
tasks.measure: Publishing consistency (100% on-schedule) and total weekly organic website visits.
tasks.mistakes: Trying to invent a brand-new topic from scratch every single morning.
tasks.example: 1 'Complete Guide to Home Espresso' article became 1 newsletter, 2 LinkedIn/IG carousels, and 3 TikTok brewing clips.

tasks.title: High-Converting Copywriting (Headlines, Ad Copy & CTAs)
tasks.what: Write clear, benefit-driven headlines and ad copy using proven frameworks like PAS (Problem -> Agitate -> Solution) and AIDA.
tasks.why: Clear words sell. Focusing on how the customer's life improves beats listing technical product specs every time.
tasks.when: Whenever writing new ads, landing pages, emails, or social captions.
tasks.tools: Tab 02 Marketing Brief & AI Prompt Helper, Google Docs, Hemingway Editor
steps: Lead with the customer's #1 desired outcome or problem in the first sentence.
Replace vague claims ('high quality service') with specific numbers ('installed in 24 hours with a 5-year warranty').
Address the top buying objection directly (shipping speed, setup ease, money-back guarantee).
Read your copy out loud—if a 12-year-old can understand it on the first read, it is ready to publish.
tasks.expected: 3 headline variations and 2 body copy options ready for A/B testing.
tasks.measure: Ad Click-Through Rate (CTR %) and Landing Page Conversion Rate (CVR %).
tasks.mistakes: Using complicated corporate buzzwords ('synergistic omnichannel solutions') instead of plain everyday language.
tasks.example: Instead of 'Next-Gen Cloud Invoicing Platform', write 'Send Invoices in 30 Seconds and Get Paid 2x Faster'.

contentPlanner.title: Review Weekly Ad Spend, Break-Even ROAS & Search Terms
contentPlanner.notes: Compare last week's spend against your Break-Even ROAS in Tab 04, block irrelevant search terms, and shift budget to top winners.

contentPlanner.title: Publish High-Intent Article & Optimize Top Landing Page
contentPlanner.channel: Website Blog + Google Search Console + GBP
contentPlanner.format: SEO Guide + Mobile Page Speed Check
contentPlanner.notes: Publish 1 helpful guide targeting a buyer keyword, add 3 internal links, and post an update on your Google Business Profile.

contentPlanner.title: Film & Schedule 3 Vertical Videos (TikTok, Reels & Shorts)
contentPlanner.notes: Hook viewers in the first 3 seconds, include clear captions in the center safe zone, and point viewers to your UTM-tagged bio link.

contentPlanner.title: Send Segmented Value Newsletter & Check Automated Flows
contentPlanner.notes: Send to engaged subscribers, check Welcome and Abandoned Cart flow click rates (focus on CTR rather than Apple MPP inflated opens).

contentPlanner.title: Review A/B Split Tests, Lead Tracker & Weekly KPI Summary
contentPlanner.channel: GA4 + Microsoft Clarity + Tab 02 Report Generator
contentPlanner.notes: Check landing page conversion rates, record A/B test results, follow up with open leads, and prepare next week's campaign brief.

contentPlanner.title: Full Campaign Rollout, UTM Tagging & Privacy Consent Check
contentPlanner.channel: Omnichannel (Paid Ads, Email, Social, Landing Page)
contentPlanner.notes: Generate clean UTM links in Tab 02, verify mobile checkout speed, confirm GDPR/privacy consent banner, and activate retargeting ads.

glossary.simple: How much gross revenue you earn back for every 1 unit of currency ($1, ₱1, £1, €1) spent on ads.
glossary.formula: ROAS = Revenue from Ads ÷ Ad Spend
glossary.example: Important: A 4.0x ROAS is NOT automatically profitable! If your product profit margin is only 20%, your break-even ROAS is 5.0x. Always compare ROAS against your Break-Even ROAS in Tab 04.

glossary.simple: The exact ROAS number you must hit so your ad campaign doesn't lose money after paying for product costs.
glossary.formula: Break-Even ROAS = 1 ÷ Gross Profit Margin (as a decimal)
glossary.example: If a product sells for $100 and costs $40 to make/deliver, your profit margin is 60% (0.60). Your Break-Even ROAS is 1 ÷ 0.60 = 1.67x.

glossary.simple: Your true profit percentage after subtracting BOTH your product/service delivery costs AND your marketing costs.
glossary.formula: ROI (%) = ((Revenue - Product Cost - Ad Spend) ÷ Total Cost) × 100
glossary.example: If you earn $10,000 in sales, product cost is $4,000, and ad spend is $2,000, your Net Profit is $4,000 and your ROI is +66.7%.

glossary.simple: Your total store revenue divided by your total ad spend across all channels combined.
glossary.formula: MER = Total Business Revenue ÷ Total Marketing Spend
glossary.example: Because customers often see a TikTok video and later search on Google, MER shows the true big-picture health of all your marketing combined.

glossary.simple: CPC is how much you pay for each click; CTR is the percentage of people who saw your ad and clicked it.
glossary.example: When your ad is relevant and has a higher CTR (e.g., 2.5% instead of 0.7%), ad platforms reward you with a lower Cost Per Click.

glossary.simple: How much marketing money you spend to win 1 paying customer.
glossary.formula: CPA = Total Ad Spend ÷ Number of New Customers
glossary.example: If your average customer brings $60 in gross profit on their first order, your CPA must stay below $60 to be profitable on day one.

glossary.simple: How much you spend to get 1 interested prospect's contact details (email, phone call, or quote request).
glossary.formula: CPL = Total Ad Spend ÷ Total Leads
glossary.example: If 1 out of every 5 leads turns into a $500 client, you can afford up to $50 per lead and still double your money.

glossary.simple: The percentage of website visitors who complete your goal (buy a product, book an appointment, or submit a form).
glossary.example: 30 buyers out of 1,000 visitors equals a 3.0% Conversion Rate.

glossary.simple: AOV is how much a buyer spends per order; LTV is the total amount they spend across all repeat orders over time.
glossary.example: Adding a 'Buy 2, Save 15%' bundle often lifts AOV from $40 to $62 immediately.

glossary.simple: Improving your website pages so they rank higher for free on Google when people search for your topic or service.
glossary.formula: Fast Mobile Page + Helpful Answer + Trusted Backlinks
glossary.example: Matching 'Search Intent' means giving a price table when someone searches 'dental braces cost', rather than a 2,000-word history of dentistry.

glossary.term: Email Open Rate & Apple Mail Privacy Protection (MPP)
glossary.simple: Open Rate shows the % of emails opened—but Apple devices often pre-load emails automatically, which inflates Open Rates.
glossary.example: Worldwide Best Practice: Always judge email success by Click Rate (CTR) and Sales/Replies, not Open Rate alone.

glossary.term: GDPR, CCPA & Data Privacy Laws (Worldwide Compliance)
glossary.simple: Laws in the UK/EU (GDPR), US (CCPA/CAN-SPAM), Philippines (DPA), and Australia that require clear user consent before tracking cookies or sending marketing emails.
glossary.formula: Clear Checkbox Consent + Cookie Banner + 1-Click Unsubscribe
glossary.example: Never buy email lists or pre-check consent boxes; always let visitors accept/decline tracking cookies and unsubscribe in 1 click.

glossary.simple: Short tags added to the end of a URL (`?utm_source=...`) so Google Analytics knows exactly which ad, email, or bio link brought the visitor.
glossary.example: Use the UTM Link Builder in Tab 02 to create clean tracking links in 5 seconds.

glossary.simple: Google's free website analytics platform that tracks how visitors find your site and which actions ('Events') they complete.
glossary.formula: Traffic Source -> Engagement -> Key Event (Purchase / Lead)
glossary.example: Marking `purchase` or `generate_lead` as a Key Event in GA4 lets you compare SEO, Email, and Paid Ads side by side.

glossary.simple: Testing one specific change (like Headline A vs. Headline B) with real traffic to prove which version gets more conversions.
glossary.formula: 1 Variable Changed + Enough Traffic (100+ conversions) = Proven Winner
glossary.example: Testing a video testimonial against a static product photo on the same audience for 7 days.

glossary.simple: Authentic videos, photos, and reviews created by real customers or creators, which build immediate trust with new shoppers.
glossary.formula: Real Customer Experience + Clear Result = Higher Trust
glossary.example: A 25-second customer unboxing video often beats an expensive studio commercial on TikTok and Instagram Reels.
